name: Mandua ki Roti
subtitle: dark finger millet flatbread, earthy and faintly sweet, soft only while hot

ingredients.note: mandua is finger millet, sold as ragi flour
for smearing; use mustard oil for a dairy-free version
for dusting, since millet dough sticks

prepNotes: Boil the water before you start. Millet has no gluten and only hot water will gelatinise the starch enough to make a workable dough.
Rest the dough 15 minutes under a cloth; it firms up and stops cracking at the edges when you pat it out.
Have the tawa heating while the dough rests, and keep a damp cloth ready to hold the finished rotis.

steps.text: Mix the ragi flour and salt in a heatproof bowl and make a well in the centre.
Pour in the boiling water all at once and stir hard with a wooden spoon for 30 seconds until it comes together as a shaggy, steaming mass.
steps.tip: Water that has gone off the boil gives a crumbly dough that will not hold a round. Use it straight from the kettle.

steps.text: Cover and leave 10 minutes, until cool enough to handle but still warm.
Knead in the bowl for 4-5 minutes with the heel of your hand until the dough is smooth, dark and slightly tacky. It should not crack when you press a ball flat.
steps.tip: Knead it warm. Cold millet dough will never come smooth however long you work it.

steps.text: Rest the dough covered with a damp cloth for 15 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls. Dust a work surface with rice flour and pat each ball out with your palm into a 15cm round about 4mm thick, turning as you go.
steps.tip: Patting by hand works far better than a rolling pin here; a pin drags and tears the dough.

steps.text: Heat a tawa over medium-high until a drop of water skitters across it.
Lay a roti on the tawa and cook 60-70 seconds until the surface dulls and small pale spots appear.
Flip and cook the second side 60 seconds, pressing the edges gently with a folded cloth until it puffs in patches and dark freckles form.
steps.tip: Millet rotis rarely balloon fully like wheat ones. Patchy puffing is the right result.

steps.text: Smear with ghee, stack in a cloth-lined box, and repeat with the rest.
Serve hot with gahat ki dal or chainsoo.

storage: Best within an hour of making. They stiffen as they cool; wrap in foil and warm on a hot tawa for 30 seconds a side. Dough keeps 1 day refrigerated, brought back to room temperature before rolling.
